title: What If You Let Go of the Space Station?

scenes.text: What if an astronaut let go of the space station? They wouldn't fall.
The station moves at about 17,500 miles an hour, so anyone letting go keeps that speed and drifts beside it.
It circles Earth every 90 minutes. For hours, you'd float next to the station, slowly drifting away.
Nothing pulls you down because you are falling around Earth, just like the station. That's why it feels weightless.
But at 250 miles up, there's still a trace of air. It drags on you, and slowly your orbit drops.
That's why the station itself needs regular reboosts. Stop them, and it would sink back to Earth too.

description:
What if you let go of the space station?
You'd keep orbiting at 17,500 miles an hour, drifting slowly away, until thin air dragged you down.
What should we run through next?
